title: Zapier consultant for CRM automation | Stacktik
metaDescription: A Zapier consultant from Stacktik builds and documents the automations between your CRM, phone, outreach and reporting tools, for a fixed fee.
h1: A Zapier consultant who documents every automation.
lede: A Zapier consultant designs and builds the automations that pass information between your tools, so a form becomes a CRM record, a call logs itself and a follow-up goes out without anyone retyping.

summary.label: What it is
summary.text: Automations between your CRM, phone, outreach and reporting tools, built with Zapier, native integrations or custom connectors, tested and documented.

summary.label: Who it is for
summary.text: Sales and customer-facing teams whose tools do not talk to each other, or whose automations were built by someone who has since left.

summary.label: What you get
summary.text: Each routine step mapped, built and tested with real examples, a written record of how it runs, a trained team and handover notes.

summary.label: How it is priced
summary.text: A fixed fee for the build, quoted in writing before work starts. Zapier stays on Zapier's own plan and pricing.

blocks.h2: CRM automation, in the steps a sales team repeats.
blocks.intro: CRM automation means the routine steps happen by rule. These are the ones Stacktik builds most often.

items.title: A form becomes a record
items.body: A web form or an inbound message creates a CRM record with the details already in, so nobody copies it across by hand.

items.title: A lead gets an owner
items.body: The new record is routed in turn, by territory, or to whoever is on duty. This is sales workflow automation at its simplest.

items.title: A call logs itself
items.body: The phone system writes the call, the recording and the notes to the right record, and a missed call becomes a callback task.

items.title: A reply stops the sequence
items.body: When a prospect answers, the outreach sequence stops and the conversation moves to a person.

items.title: A signed deal moves the stage
items.body: A signature or a payment updates the deal and starts the handover to the next team.

items.title: The numbers update themselves
items.body: The dashboard and the revenue scoreboard pull from the CRM, the phone system and the outreach tool without anyone typing.

blocks.h2: When Zapier is the right tool, and when it is not.
blocks.intro: Zapier is one of three ways to connect two tools.

items.title: The vendor's own integration
items.body: When two tools already integrate, use that first. It is maintained by the vendor and usually carries more detail than a general connector can.

items.title: Zapier, for the gaps
items.body: Zapier fits a simple step between two tools that have no integration of their own.

items.title: A custom connector
items.body: When a step needs logic a connector cannot express, or the tool has no integration at all, Stacktik builds the connector itself.

items.title: An AI agent, where judgement is needed
items.body: A rule cannot decide what a message means. We build an AI agent on Claude or OpenAI, with a person approving anything that reaches a customer.

items.title: Fewer automations, well documented
items.body: Every automation is something to maintain. We build the ones that earn their place and write each one down.

blocks.h2: How Stacktik builds CRM workflow automation.
blocks.intro: One technical RevOps consultant is assigned to your project and stays with it.

items.title: A free call
items.body: We go through how leads, calls and follow-ups move through your team today, what you use, and what isn't working.

items.title: A written proposal
items.body: What to keep, connect or replace, the monthly cost of each tool, and our fee for the work, fixed before it starts.

items.title: Map each step
items.body: For each automation we write down what starts it, what it reads, what it changes and what a correct result looks like.

items.title: Build and test
items.body: The automation is built in your own accounts through a seat you control, and tested with real examples before it runs on live records.

items.title: Document, train and hand over
items.body: Each automation is written up: what it does, where it lives and how to change it. Your team is trained, and the notes are yours.

platforms.intro: Zapier sits between other tools. These are the CRM, calling, outreach, AI and reporting platforms Stacktik sets up and connects.

faq.q: What does a Zapier consultant do?
faq.a: A Zapier consultant maps the routine steps between your tools, builds the automations that carry them out, tests them and documents how they run. Stacktik's consultant also tells you when a native integration, a custom connector or an AI agent is the better route.

CRM automation is having the CRM and the tools around it carry out routine steps by rule: creating a record from a form, assigning an owner, logging a call, stopping a sequence on a reply, updating a deal stage. It removes the retyping, not the judgement.

faq.q: How much does a Zapier consultant cost?
faq.a: Stacktik quotes the build as a fixed fee in writing before work starts, based on how many steps are automated and how many tools they touch. Zapier itself stays on Zapier's own plan and pricing. Nothing is charged for the first call.

Stacktik is a RevOps consultancy that uses Zapier as one of several tools. We are not tied to it. If the vendor's own integration or a custom connector does the job better, that is what goes on the proposal.

faq.q: Can you fix automations someone else built?
faq.a: Yes. We list what each automation does, test it against real records, remove the ones that conflict or no longer matter, and document the rest so your team can maintain them.

faq.q: Which Zapier integrations do you set up most?
faq.a: The ones around the CRM: forms and lead sources into the CRM, the phone system, email and LinkedIn outreach tools, conversation notes, and reporting. Each connection is tested with real examples and written down.

closeH2: Start with one step someone retypes.
closeLede: A free call about the tools you use and what still gets done by hand.
